metadata.case_name: WONG SHIU PING v. SECRETARY FOR JUSTICE FOR AND ON BEHALF OF THE DIRECTOR OF LEISURE AND CULTURAL SERVICE

plaintiff.occupation_before: Previously worked as a cook and a hawker; during retirement sometimes worked as a casual worker doing odd jobs (substitute waiter or cook, distributing leaflets, shop assistant)

injuries.description: 10 cm laceration wound on forehead; wound closed by suturing with 9 stitches
source: Amongst other injuries, he sustained a 10 cm laceration wound on his forehead.
The wound over his head was closed by suturing with 9 stitches.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

source: In the joint medical report of Dr Fu Wai Kee and Dr Poon Kai Ming, both experts agree with the diagnosis of head concussion following the Accident.

injuries.description: Mild scalp soft tissue swelling at the right frontal aspect
source: On that occasion, CT scan of the brain was done which revealed mild scalp soft tissue swelling at the right frontal aspect.

injuries.description: Minor soft tissue injury of the left shoulder (recovered fully)
source: Both experts however agree that the plaintiff has sustained minor soft tissue injury of the left shoulder as a result of the accident.
It is agreed that the plaintiff has recovered fully from the left shoulder injury.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of unspecified muscle, fascia or tendon at shoulder or upper arm level

manifestations.description: numbness sensation over his right leg
pins and needles sensations over his body
loss of consciousness immediately after the Accident
mild scalp soft tissue swelling at the right frontal aspect

source: The wound over his head was closed by suturing with 9 stitches.

treatments_received.treatment: admitted to the emergency medical ward for observation
source: He was admitted to the emergency medical ward for further observation. He was discharged on the next day.
On that occasion, CT scan of the brain was done which revealed mild scalp soft tissue swelling at the right frontal aspect.

treatments_received.treatment: follow-up treatment at government clinics (Department of Family Medicine and Primary Health Care of Chai Wan Health Centre)
source: The plaintiff attended the Department of Family Medicine and Primary Health Care of Chai Wan Health Centre on 19 October 2011.
For the treatments received by the plaintiff at the government hospital and clinics, those expenses were supported by the medical reports and/or receipts.

treatments_received.treatment: treatment by a Chinese medical practitioner in the Mainland
source: The medical expenses mainly consisted a sum of $45,000 as medical treatments received from the Chinese medical practitioner based in the Mainland.
